headline: Gulf Shores condo insurance for Orange Beach and Baldwin County owners
body: Gulf Shores condo insurance, explained: how an HO-6 fits the HOA master policy, loss assessment, flood, wind and rentals in Orange Beach and Baldwin County.
label: SWIPE

slides.t: HO-6, sometimes written HO6, is the common name for a condominium unit-owners policy. It can cover the parts of the unit you are responsible for under the condo documents. It can also cover your belongings, personal liability, loss of use and loss assessment.

slides.h: Does the HOA master policy cover my condo unit?
slides.t: It depends on the master policy and the condo documents. Some master policies cover only the bare structure, some include original interior finishes, and some include improvements too.

slides.h: What is loss assessment coverage on a condo policy?
slides.t: Loss assessment coverage may help pay an owner's share when the association assesses unit owners for a covered loss. One example is the association's deductible after a storm. It pays up to the limit, subject to the policy's terms.

slides.h: Do I need flood insurance for a Gulf Shores or Orange Beach condo?
slides.t: Flood is generally excluded from condo unit-owners policies. Some HOAs carry flood coverage on the building through the National Flood Insurance Program. Unit owners can also consider their own flood policy for contents and their share of the unit.

slides.h: What affects the cost of condo insurance in Gulf Shores?
slides.t: Several things affect what you pay. They include the building's age and construction, how close it is to the water, and what the master policy covers.
